title: Cross-stream graph consistency and automated recovery for interrupted prefill/replay
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: We intermittently observe incorrect outputs or CUDA errors when a prefill capture is interrupted (preempt, driver hiccup, or competing stream synchronization) and a multi-stream replay resumes. Root cause analysis points to inconsistent ephemeral allocator state and mismatched kernel selection metadata across streams during replay. This ticket implements a set of guardrails and an automated reconciliation path to ensure cross-stream graph consistency and provide a safe rollback/fallback when full deterministic replay cannot be guaranteed.

Goals:
- Detect divergence between captured graph expectations and current device/stream state before replay.
- Provide a lightweight reconciliation phase that replays only idempotent warmup ops to reestablish KV cache and allocator invariants.
- When reconciliation cannot be performed safely, gracefully fall back to single-stream decode or CPU decode for the affected request(s) to maintain correctness.
- Add runtime instrumentation and capture-diff logs to make root-cause reproducible in CI and customer debugging.

Design approach / Implementation plan:
1) Capture metadata enrichment (non-invasive): record a small deterministic header alongside CUDA graph captures that includes: kernel selection hash, allocator watermark, stream-affinity-map, and expected prefill-length. This header is ~128B and stored in the capture cache.
2) Pre-replay validation: before invoking cudaGraphLaunch, compare current runtime state vs captured header. If hashes and allocator watermark match -> proceed. If low-risk mismatches (e.g., allocator watermark within small tolerance, same kernels but different minor tuning), trigger reconciliation path.
3) Reconciliation path (idempotent warmup): run a compact sequence of the original prefill ops in a special affinity-bound stream with deterministic padding and no side-effects (no updates to non-ephemeral globals). This establishes expected KV cache and allocator shape. After warmup, re-validate headers and proceed to graph replay.
4) Safe fallback: if reconciliation fails or times out, mark capture as tainted for this request and route to single-stream decode on a dedicated fallback worker (with higher CPU/GPU cost but preserves correctness). Emit audit event and increment fallback metric.
5) Instrumentation & debugging: produce a "capture-diff" artifact (text diff and JSON header snapshot) uploaded to the request trace and available in console for engineers/customers. Add a server-side sampling flag to upload full device allocations for triage.
6) CI / e2e tests: add a test harness that simulates interrupted prefill with configurable allocator offsets and driver errors. Verify correctness across 1000 randomized seeds and assert <0.5% correctness regression vs baseline.

Tradeoffs and risks:
- Extra pre-replay validation and reconciliation adds small latency for cold captures; we will gate this with heuristics (only runs when mismatch detected or when capture age > threshold).
- Fallback to single-stream decode increases cost for affected requests; we will track and throttle fallbacks to avoid runaway costs.
- Complexity in allocator watermarking: requires deterministic behavior of ephemeral allocator; mitigation is to use a conservative watermark and make reconciliation idempotent.

Metrics / Success criteria:
- Reduce captured-replay-related customer errors by >= 90% for multi-stream workloads.
- Fallback rate < 1% of requests for normally healthy fleets.
- End-to-end median latency impact for healthy captures < +1ms; for reconciliations < +10ms.

Artifacts / Links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRV/Cross-stream+Graph+Consistency+Design
- PR (implementation draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- Repro harness: //github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/tree/main/test/graph_replay_harness

Next steps / owner tasks:
- Implement capture header writer/reader (Liam)
- Add pre-replay validator and reconciliation runner (Maya + Samir)
- Integrate capture-diff artifact upload into tracing pipeline (Observability team)
- Add CI fault-injection scenarios (QA and Infra)
acceptance_criteria: Pre-replay validator implemented and unit-tested (header comparisons + tolerance checks)
Reconciliation runner that can reestablish KV cache deterministically for at least two model families (GPT-like, encoder-decoder)
Fallback path executed and verified in harness when reconciliation intentionally fails
Capture-diff artifacts appear in sampled traces and include kernel-hash + allocator snapshot
E2E CI test simulating mid-capture interruption passes across 1000 randomized seeds
Fallout / customer-facing errors related to graph replay reduced by >= 90% in canary fleet
